title: Late-Release Interest Rate Tied to the Contract APR
content:
# Late-Release Interest Rate Tied to the Contract APR

Under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda, the yearly rate at which late-release interest runs on a refund released to the lienholder follows the contract APR of the waiver's purchase deal, as printed on the installment contract recorded in the Vehicle Purchase Agreements records. A contract APR is read as a yearly rate: the printed APR divided by 100 (a printed 7.25 is a yearly rate of 0.0725).

## Rate schedule

| Contract APR on the waiver's purchase deal | Yearly rate the late-release interest runs at |
|---|---|
| Above 0.09 (above 9 percent) | 0.09 |
| Above 0.05 and no more than 0.09 | That contract APR |
| 0.05 or less, 0.00 included, or no contract APR on the deal | 0.05 |

## Boundaries

- A printed APR of exactly 9.00 is no more than 0.09, so the interest runs at that APR, 0.09; a printed 9.01 is above it and the rate is held at 0.09.
- A printed APR of exactly 5.00 falls in the bottom band, so the rate is 0.05; a printed 5.01 runs at 0.0501.
- A deal that carries no contract APR, or a printed 0.00, runs at 0.05.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A refund due of 980.40 is released 22 days past the refund payment period, and the waiver's purchase deal shows a printed APR of 7.25. The rate is 0.0725, so the late-release interest is 980.40 times 0.0725 times 22, divided by 365, which is 4.284…, rounded half up to 4.28. On a deal with a printed APR of 3.90 the same release runs at 0.05 and the interest is 2.95.
